chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Fadhl from Marwan ibn Muslim from Ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who paid the zakat of his wealth, one thousand dirhams, but could not find a place to give it to, so he looked at a slave being sold and whoever offered more, so he bought him with that one thousand dirhams which he had paid from his zakat, and he freed him. Is that permissible? He said, 'Yes, there is no harm with that.' I said to him, 'For when he was freed and became free, he traded and practiced a profession, acquired wealth, then died and had no heir. So who will inherit him if he has no heir?' He said, 'The poor believers who are entitled to zakat will inherit him, because he was purchased with their money.'
ai.seo_question: Who inherits the estate of a freed slave if he dies without heirs after being purchased with zakat funds?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a mechanism for zakat distribution when direct recipients are unavailable, permitting the purchase and manumission of a slave as a valid substitute. This ruling highlights the concept of 'substitution' in Shia jurisprudence, where the funds retain their sacred status as the property of the poor, thereby entitling them to inherit the freed slave's estate upon death without heirs.
